topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, sets the context within the cancer lecture series, and outlines the core learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Causes of Cancer: Genetics, Environmental Factors, and Chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental drivers of cancer development, comparing endogenous cellular errors and inherited predispositions with environmental exposures and epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Biological and Chemical Carcinogens and Mechanisms of DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific infectious, physical, dietary, and chemical carcinogens and explain the metabolic and molecular mechanisms by which they induce DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, detailing the initiator-promoter model, inflammation-driven growth, and tissue susceptibility during specific developmental stages.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental methods used to determine whether agents cause cancer and discuss their practical limitations.
